Be where someone needs you before they have to ask.

These techniques require a held shield. Reductions apply after resistance and respect the minimum for attacks, except immunity. Use your ordinary Reaction for reactive techniques. Protection never supplies an extra defense roll or stacks copies of the same technique. All movement requires legal routes and destinations.

Shieldwork

Shield Bash I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Brawn. Attack one adjacent creature with your shield for 1/2/3 physical damage. On Standard or Strong, push it 1 square directly away. Resolve collisions normally.

Shield Bash II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Shield Bash deals 2/3/4 physical damage.

Shield Bash III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Shield Bash also knocks its target Prone on Strong after the push.

Break the Line I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Brawn. Attack up to two adjacent enemies. Roll once; each takes 1/2/3 physical damage and is pushed 1 square directly away. Resolve collisions normally.

Break the Line II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Break the Line deals 2/3/4 physical damage.

Break the Line III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Break the Line pushes 2 squares instead of 1; on Strong each target also becomes Prone.

Shatter the Formation

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Brawn, with a melee weapon and shield. Attack up to three adjacent enemies. Roll once; each takes 2/4/6 physical damage and is pushed up to 2 squares directly away. On Strong each also becomes Prone. Blocked movement stops the push, not damage or Prone; resolve collisions normally. Each target is struck once.

Shelter

Sheltering Guard I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver. Choose one willing adjacent ally. Until your next turn starts it gains 1 Boon on ranged defenses while adjacent. Reusing this technique replaces its previous effect. No roll.

Sheltering Guard II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Sheltering Guard can protect two adjacent allies.

Sheltering Guard III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Sheltering Guard also gives each protected ally Stability 1 while adjacent.

Shield Canopy I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver. Until your next turn starts, you and up to three willing adjacent allies reduce ranged attack damage by 2 after resistance while they remain adjacent. Reusing this technique replaces its previous effect. No roll.

Shield Canopy II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 When you use Shield Canopy, you may first move 1 square toward an ally without movement reactions; choose protected allies after moving.

Shield Canopy III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Shield Canopy also gives its protected creatures 1 Boon on melee defense while they remain adjacent.

The Moving Bulwark

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver. Once per scene, choose up to four willing allies within 3 squares who can perceive your signal. You and each chosen ally may move 2 squares without movement reactions. Until your next turn starts, you and chosen allies within 3 squares gain 1 Boon on defense and reduce attack damage by 3 after resistance. Leaving range suspends the protection until returning. No roll.

Interception

Interpose I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction. After an adjacent ally rolls defense, before applying physical damage from that attack, reduce that damage by 1 after resistance. You must be able to reach the ally. No roll.

Interpose II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Interpose reduces physical damage by 2.

Interpose III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Before Interpose you may move 1 square to reach the ally without movement reactions.

Take the Blow I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction. Before an adjacent ally rolls defense against a single-target attack, become its target if the attacker can legally target you. Roll your defense and receive all effects; the ally receives none.

Take the Blow II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Before Take the Blow you may move up to 2 squares without movement reactions to reach an ally within 2 squares. Become a legal target before substituting.

Take the Blow III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 When you use Take the Blow, gain 1 Boon on your defense. After the intercepted attack resolves, the attacker’s remaining voluntary movement this turn becomes 0. Forced movement still applies.

The Last Safe Step

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Reaction. When an ally within 4 squares is about to take damage from an attack or fall, move up to 4 squares to reach it. If you reach it, move together up to 2 more squares and reduce that damage by 4 after resistance. Neither creature triggers movement reactions during this rescue. An attack still resolves against its original target; a fall ends only if the destination supports both creatures. Fall damage can reach 0. No roll beyond the original defense.

Watchfulness

Guarded Passage I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction. Before an adjacent ally rolls defense against a reaction triggered by its movement, grant that defense 1 Boon. No roll.

Guarded Passage II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Guarded Passage grants 2 Boons instead of 1.

Guarded Passage III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Guarded Passage also reduces damage from that reaction by 1 after resistance.

Rescue Step I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver. Move up to 2 squares to a willing ally, then move with it up to 2 more squares. Both creatures ignore movement reactions during this movement and finish adjacent. You can carry a helpless ally no larger than you instead, with a free hand and normal carrying limits. No roll.

Rescue Step II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Rescue Step’s initial approach may cover 3 squares instead of 2.

Rescue Step III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Rescue Step may escort two willing allies together, each starting and finishing adjacent to you; alternatively carry one helpless ally as before.

The Long Road

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action. Once per scene, guide up to four willing allies initially within 3 squares along legal routes up to 6 squares each, moving up to 6 squares yourself. All ignore movement reactions and must finish within 3 squares of you. Instead of one willing traveler, carry a helpless creature no larger than you, without additional encumbrance for this move; place it adjacent afterward. This does not heal or stabilize. No roll.

Open a door, steady a friend or turn a room.

Use social objectives: the DA decides credible approaches, attainable concessions and what completes an exchange. A roll changes progress, never another player’s decisions. Another roll requires a new fact, offer or changed circumstance. Brief appeals can fit a Main Action; negotiations take the time their conversation needs. Use a Reaction when its stated trigger occurs during the exchange.

Negotiation

Make the Case I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Reason for a brief appeal, or one exchange for a longer discussion. Present a credible argument or offer to someone who understands you; add 1/2/3 progress toward the social objective established by the DA.

Make the Case II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Make the Case adds 1/3/4 progress.

Make the Case III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Once per objective, add 1 extra progress to Make the Case when you answer a listener’s concern with a new fact, concrete offer or demonstration.

Common Ground I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Reason for a brief proposal, or one exchange for detailed terms. Propose common terms to two willing negotiating sides who understand you. Roll once; add 1/2/3 progress to each side’s separate acceptance objective. Each side retains its established boundaries.

Common Ground II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Common Ground adds 1/3/4 progress to each objective.

Common Ground III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Common Ground can address three willing negotiating sides with separate objectives.

A Treaty in Common Words

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 30 minutes · Reason. With willing representatives of up to three sides and a working language, interpreter or shared reference text, formulate one concrete agreement. Roll once; add 3/5/7 progress to each side’s acceptance objective. On completion the DA states that side’s commitments and known reservations plainly. A shared reference permits simple terms; complex terms need adequate translation. No side accepts impossible terms, and the agreement is not magical enforcement.

Leadership

Steady Voice I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver. One willing ally within 4 squares who hears and understands your reassurance reduces Frightened by 1. No roll.

Steady Voice II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Steady Voice reduces Frightened by 2.

Steady Voice III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Steady Voice affects two willing allies within range.

Rally the Line I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver. Up to three willing allies within 6 squares who perceive and understand your signal reduce Frightened by 2. One of them may also move 1 square toward you without movement reactions. No roll.

Rally the Line II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Rally the Line can affect four allies.

Rally the Line III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Each ally affected by Rally the Line may move 1 square toward you without movement reactions.

Hold the Company Together

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver. Once per scene, up to four willing allies within 6 squares who perceive and understand you reduce Frightened and Dazed by 2 each, gain 1 Boon on their next defense before your next turn starts, and may move 2 squares toward you without movement reactions. This grants no additional actions or Reactions. No roll.

Rejoinder

Plausible Rejoinder I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction · Guile. When a listener who understands you challenges your account or questions your distraction, answer before its response resolves; add 1/2/3 progress toward the DA’s deception objective. Once per distinct challenge per exchange. You may also present an ordinary plausible false account during an exchange using the same progress; repetition and impossible claims earn no progress.

Plausible Rejoinder II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Plausible Rejoinder adds 1/3/4 progress.

Plausible Rejoinder III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Once per objective, add 1 extra progress to Plausible Rejoinder when you give the listener a new reason to believe the account, such as a telling detail, prop or supporting witness.

Hold Their Attention I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction · Guile. When up to three listeners within 6 squares who understand you begin to turn attention from your ongoing plausible distraction, renew it with a new detail before they act. Add 1/2/3 progress toward holding their attention for one minute. On completion allies gain 1 Boon on unnoticed tasks outside those listeners’ direct sight for that minute. Once per distinct interruption; you may also begin this distraction through an ordinary exchange.

Hold Their Attention II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Hold Their Attention adds 1/3/4 progress.

Hold Their Attention III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Hold Their Attention can engage five listeners; an immediate obvious danger ends its distraction.

Turn the Conversation

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Reaction · Guile. Once per conversation, when listeners are about to dismiss your distraction or false account, offer a credible alternative explanation before they act. Roll once; add 3/5/7 progress to up to four listeners’ separate objectives for accepting it. Each completed objective keeps that listener engaged for one minute, giving allies 2 Boons on unnoticed tasks outside its sight during that time. Contradictory proof and impossible explanations cannot be talked away; direct danger ends the distraction.

Pressure

Draw the Line I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · One exchange · Brawn. State a credible immediate consequence you can carry out to a listener who perceives and understands the threat; add 1/2/3 progress toward a limited concession established by the DA.

Draw the Line II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Draw the Line adds 1/3/4 progress.

Draw the Line III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Once per objective, add 1 extra progress to Draw the Line when you show or explain how you could carry out the consequence without attacking the listener.

Terms of Surrender I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Reason. Offer a feasible surrender to up to three enemies who understand you. Roll once; add 1/2/3 progress to their shared objective if they share a motive, otherwise to one chosen enemy’s objective. They continue acting until an objective completes.

Terms of Surrender II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Terms of Surrender adds 1/3/4 progress.

Terms of Surrender III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Terms of Surrender can address six enemies with a shared motive; otherwise choose one as before.

A Way to Yield

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Reason. Once per scene, offer a credible, immediately available path out of a conflict to up to six enemies who understand you: surrender under stated protection, withdraw through an open route, or release captives for safe passage. Roll once; add 3/5/7 progress to their shared objective if their motives align, otherwise one chosen enemy’s objective. On completion they accept the established concession while you honor its terms. This grants no automatic ceasefire before completion and no control over independent allies.

Contact beings, establish bonds and cross boundaries.

Begin studying this discipline for the DP price printed for your class, then choose one of its four spellbooks. Learn the book’s sections in order, adding their spells to your repertoire.

Restore, transform, cultivate and unravel living things.

Begin studying this discipline for the DP price printed for your class, then choose one of its four spellbooks. Learn the book’s sections in order, adding their spells to your repertoire.

  • @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.9fd41e62dec3874f]{Serevan’s Book of Restoration}.

  • @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.92ab59bd0e5155f5]{Serevan’s Book of Growth}.

Find the line between your hand and a distant mark.

Each attack requires a ready ranged weapon and ammunition or a held thrown weapon. Spend one projectile per target unless the technique says otherwise; a thrown weapon stays where it lands. Choose visible targets within the technique’s stated reach. Basic Ranged and Basic Throw can reach farther using the ordinary weapon range rule. Improvements affect only their named technique.

Precision

Measured Shot I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Agility. Attack one creature within 8 squares for 2/3/5 physical damage.

Measured Shot II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Measured Shot deals 3/4/6 physical damage.

Measured Shot III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Measured Shot has range 12 squares.

Split the Flight I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Agility. Attack up to three creatures within 8 squares. Roll once; each takes 1/2/4 physical damage. Each is struck once.

Split the Flight II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Split the Flight has range 12 squares.

Split the Flight III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Split the Flight deals 2/3/5 physical damage. You may also spend a Main Action observing one visible creature within 12 squares to mark a vulnerable part of its anatomy or construction for this scene; no roll. The DA identifies a plausible exposed part, or states that none is visible.

Anatomist’s Volley

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Agility. Attack up to three enemies within 12 squares. Roll once. Each takes 3/5/8 physical damage. For a target whose vulnerable part you know from Split the Flight’s study or evidence, apply that hit ignoring up to 2 physical resistance. Apply immunity and other reductions normally.

Pinning

Hobbling Aim I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver. Choose one visible creature within 8 squares. Your next Main Action ranged or thrown attack against it before this turn ends also applies Slowed 1 on Standard or Strong. This modifies one target of one attack. Reusing this technique replaces its unused effect.

Hobbling Aim II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 On Strong, Hobbling Aim applies Slowed 2 instead of 1.

Hobbling Aim III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 On Weak, Hobbling Aim also applies Slowed 1.

Hold the Pass I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver. Choose up to two visible creatures within 8 squares. Before your turn ends, your next Main Action ranged or thrown attack applies Slowed 1 to each chosen creature it attacks, on any result. This grants no extra targets or attacks and replaces Hobbling Aim for that attack.

Hold the Pass II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Hold the Pass can choose creatures within 12 squares.

Hold the Pass III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Hold the Pass applies Slowed 2 instead of 1 to those targets.

Close the Escape

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver. Once per scene, choose up to three visible creatures within 12 squares. Your next Main Action ranged or thrown attack this turn applies Slowed 2 to each chosen creature it attacks; on Strong their voluntary movement becomes 0 until the end of their next turns. Forced movement still applies. This replaces Hold the Pass or Hobbling Aim on that attack and grants no extra targets.

Readiness

Watchful Shot I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction · Agility. When a visible enemy within 6 squares finishes voluntary movement, attack it for 1/2/3 physical damage after that movement.

Watchful Shot II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Watchful Shot has range 8 squares.

Watchful Shot III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Watchful Shot deals 1/2/4 physical damage. It can also respond when a visible enemy finishes forced movement within range.

Covering Fire I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction · Agility. When an ally within 4 squares begins voluntary movement, attack one visible enemy within 8 squares for 1/2/4 physical damage before that movement. That ally’s first 2 squares of this movement trigger no reactions from that enemy.

Covering Fire II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Covering Fire has attack range 12 squares and can protect an ally within 6 squares.

Covering Fire III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Covering Fire deals 2/3/5 physical damage and protects that ally’s first 3 squares from the target’s movement reactions.

Hunt at the Crossroads

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 10 minutes. Prepare an ambush along a trail you have followed, at a site you have surveyed by actually examining its routes and sight lines. Choose up to four willing allies and a visible trigger line up to 6 squares long. Once before your next safe overnight rest, when a tracked enemy crosses the line, you and each chosen ally may spend an available Reaction to make one known basic attack against it if in range. These attacks gain 1 Boon and +2 damage. Preparation ends if you leave the site. Resolve awareness and initiative normally; preparation grants no additional surprise turn.

Thrown Weapons

Hurl I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Agility. Throw one held weapon at a creature within 4 squares for 2/3/5 physical damage.

Hurl II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Hurl has range 6 squares.

Hurl III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 After Hurl, draw one accessible replacement weapon without spending an action. This does not retrieve the thrown weapon.

Ricochet I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Agility. Throw one weapon at two creatures within 4 squares of you and 2 squares of each other. Roll once; each takes 1/2/4 physical damage. The weapon lands beside the second target.

Ricochet II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Ricochet has range 6 squares from you; its targets must still be within 2 squares of each other.

Ricochet III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Ricochet deals 2/3/5 physical damage to each target.

Steel across the Gap

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Agility. Jump up to 4 squares to a visible legal landing without movement reactions. At any point during the jump, throw one held weapon at up to two visible enemies within 6 squares of you and 2 squares of each other. Roll once; each takes 3/5/7 physical damage. The weapon lands beside the second target, or beside the only target if there is one.

Recognize hurt, and work patiently to ease it.

Carry suitable medical supplies. First aid allows one attempt per recipient between safe overnight rests, shared across all healers; a healing technique uses that attempt when used, not only on a favorable result. HP never exceeds maximum. Condition care is separate. Willing or helpless patients can receive care; healing and stabilization use the ordinary death-tally rules. Reactions occur before the stated roll or consequence.

First Aid

Field Dressing I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action, with a free hand and bandaging: reduce an adjacent patient’s Bleeding by 2, minimum 0, without HP restoration or a first-aid attempt. Alternatively spend 10 minutes and roll Knowledge to restore 3/5/7 HP to a patient within reach, consuming its first-aid attempt.

Field Dressing II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Field Dressing’s first aid restores 4/6/8 HP; its immediate bandaging reduces Bleeding by 3.

Field Dressing III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Field Dressing’s first aid takes 5 minutes. Its bandaging can be performed as a Maneuver.

Emergency Treatment I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Knowledge, with medical supplies. Apply Field Dressing’s current healing immediately to an adjacent patient and mark its first-aid attempt used.

Emergency Treatment II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Emergency Treatment restores 5/7/9 HP instead of Field Dressing’s amount.

Emergency Treatment III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Emergency Treatment also reduces Bleeding by 2, and you may move 1 square toward the patient before treating it without movement reactions.

A Way through Death

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Knowledge, with medical supplies. Move up to 3 squares to a patient no larger than you, restore 5/8/11 HP using its available first-aid attempt, then carry it up to 3 squares and place it in a legal adjacent square. Both movements ignore movement reactions. You may rescue a patient whose allowance is spent without healing or consuming supplies. A free hand is needed to carry it; no armor training is required.

Nursing

Patient Care I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver. With suitable water, blankets or other supplies and a free hand, reduce temporary Burning or Freezing on one adjacent patient by 2, minimum 0. No roll, HP restoration or first-aid attempt.

Patient Care II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Patient Care reduces the chosen condition by 3.

Patient Care III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Patient Care treats two adjacent patients with supplies for both.

Ready the Remedy I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver. Administer one prepared medical remedy you carry to an adjacent patient, using its printed effect. It must be a remedy ordinarily administered as a Main Action, not a spell, ritual or healing potion. Alternatively apply Patient Care and give that patient 1 Boon on its next Fortitude roll against an existing nonmagical disease before your next turn ends. No additional roll.

Ready the Remedy II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 After Ready the Remedy administers a prepared dose, also reduce the patient’s temporary Bleeding by 1 with suitable bandaging.

Ready the Remedy III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Ready the Remedy can administer two prepared doses to two different adjacent patients in the same Maneuver, consuming each dose. Each may also receive its bleeding care.

Watch through the Night

DP: 5 | Level: 7 During a safe overnight rest, spend your two quiet hours tending up to four willing patients with suitable supplies. Each gains 2 Boons on its next Fortitude roll against an existing nonmagical disease before its next safe overnight rest, and reduces temporary Poisoned by 2 at the end of this care. Each patient benefits once per rest. Normal sleep, healing and recovery requirements remain; this is not an additional rest.

Resuscitation

Keep Them Breathing I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction. Before an adjacent living creature rolls a death roll, support its breathing with a free hand and grant that roll 1 Boon. Apply its result normally. No extra roll or healing.

Keep Them Breathing II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Keep Them Breathing grants 2 Boons.

Keep Them Breathing III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Before Keep Them Breathing, move 1 square to reach the patient without movement reactions.

Hold the Moment I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction. When a living patient within 2 squares is about to make a death roll, move up to 2 squares to reach it without movement reactions and use a free hand to grant that roll 2 Boons. After the roll, reduce its Bleeding by 2 with suitable bandaging. This spends one Reaction and does not grant another death roll.

Hold the Moment II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Hold the Moment can reach a patient within 3 squares by moving up to 3 squares.

Hold the Moment III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Hold the Moment also reduces temporary Burning or Freezing by 2 after the death roll if you have appropriate water or insulating supplies.

One More Chance

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Reaction · Knowledge. Once per safe overnight rest, when an adjacent living creature would receive its third death-failure mark, use a free hand and medical supplies before death resolves. Roll: on Weak it gains the mark normally; on Standard it remains Dying at two failure marks without adding the triggering mark; on Strong stabilize it at 0 HP, clearing both death tallies as normal. This provides no HP or Grit and cannot affect an already dead creature. A patient can benefit from this named intervention only once between its safe overnight rests, regardless of healer.

Diagnosis

Read the Symptoms I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · 10 minutes · Knowledge. Examine a patient with observable symptoms or a sample; add 1/2/3 progress toward identifying a nonmagical disease or toxin and a plausible remedy.

Read the Symptoms II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Read the Symptoms adds 1/3/4 progress.

Read the Symptoms III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Read the Symptoms takes 5 minutes per attempt.

Prepare the Remedy I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · 1 hour · Knowledge, with ingredients appropriate to a diagnosed toxin. Prepare one dose by adding 1/2/3 progress to the DA’s preparation objective. Administer the completed dose as a Main Action to reduce that toxin’s Poisoned by 2. Consume it on use. Other disease effects require their stated remedy.

Prepare the Remedy II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Prepare the Remedy adds 1/3/4 progress.

Prepare the Remedy III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Prepare the Remedy’s dose reduces its toxin’s Poisoned by 3 instead of 2.

The Field Hospital

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 30 minutes, with medical supplies and a safe prepared shelter. Treat up to six patients, using each available first-aid attempt. Roll Knowledge once; each restores 5/8/11 HP and reduces temporary Bleeding or Poisoned by 2, choosing separately per patient. A patient with a spent allowance receives condition care only. Supplies must cover all patients. This creates no extra first-aid allowance, SP recovery or overnight rest.

Thought, feeling, perception and the dreaming mind.

Ask the question that turns an old fact into a useful one.

Bring a question and the evidence you can examine. The DA sets the objective and gives truthful findings supported by that evidence, including what remains uncertain. After completing an investigation, pursue a new question or new evidence. Learn spells and recipes through their own study requirements.

Investigation

Read the Evidence I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Reason. Examine one accessible clue within reach; add 1/2/3 progress toward a concrete question about it. Searching a scene instead takes 10 minutes per attempt. You may also recall a relevant fact about a subject or reliable description: 1 minute, Knowledge, 1/2/3 progress toward a question set before rolling.

Read the Evidence II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Read the Evidence adds 1/3/4 progress to examination, scene searches and recall.

Read the Evidence III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Read the Evidence takes 5 minutes per scene-search attempt; recalling a fact takes a Main Action.

Reconstruct the Scene I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Reason to compare up to three accessible clues, or 10 minutes to reconstruct a larger scene you can examine. Add 1/2/3 progress toward the order of up to three related events. On completion the DA states supported conclusions and gaps; this reveals no unseen thoughts.

Reconstruct the Scene II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Reconstruct the Scene adds 1/3/4 progress.

Reconstruct the Scene III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Reconstruct the Scene may connect up to five related events, with 1 Boon when at least two independent sources corroborate the sequence.

The Truth before the Council

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 10 minutes · Reason. Present your findings and their supporting evidence to up to four decision-makers who understand you. Use testimony, records, exhibits or an explanation of what you found. Roll once; add 3/5/7 progress to each relevant acceptance objective. On completion a listener acknowledges the supported facts and grants the attainable concession established with the DA. Unsupported claims and inaccessible facts remain unproven.

Planning

Survey the Ground I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver · Reason. Study one visible approach within 6 squares; add 1/2/3 progress toward identifying its usable footing and visible hazards. Surveying a whole site takes 10 minutes per attempt instead. Concealed threats require evidence to discover.

Survey the Ground II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Survey the Ground adds 1/3/4 progress.

Survey the Ground III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Survey the Ground also reveals one feasible fallback route when its objective completes, if one exists.

Prepared Retreat I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver. Once per scene, direct up to three willing allies within 6 squares along a visible or familiar fallback route. Each immediately moves 2 squares without movement reactions. They must perceive your instructions; changed or blocked routes provide no passage. No roll.

Prepared Retreat II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Prepared Retreat may direct four allies and lets each move 3 squares.

Prepared Retreat III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 You can also spend a Maneuver to point out an opening against a visible enemy to up to three allies within 6 squares. Each ally who perceives your cue gains 1 Boon on its next attack against that enemy before your next turn ends. Once per creature per scene. This grants no extra attacks or targets.

Name the Decisive Weakness

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver. Once per creature per scene, describe an opening in a visible enemy’s stance, construction or tactics. Up to four allies within 6 squares who perceive your explanation gain 2 Boons on their next attack against it before your next turn ends; each such attack ignores 1 point of one matching resistance. Immunity remains. Use this benefit in place of Prepared Retreat’s attack Boon for that creature.

Disputation

Counterexample I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction. Before a listener within 6 squares rolls to assess a claim, ask a question or talk through the claim with them. If the listener understands you, give that roll 1 Boon. Once per distinct claim. No roll of your own.

Counterexample II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Counterexample grants 2 Boons.

Counterexample III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Counterexample may aid two listeners assessing the same claim, before their rolls. Reaction: before an ally within 6 squares rolls defense against an attack you can perceive, point out the danger. If the ally understands you, give that defense 1 Boon. Once per attacker per scene.

Correct the Record I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction · Knowledge. When a listener within 6 squares is about to act on a factual error, explain what it has missed before it acts. Add 1/2/3 progress to the DA’s objective for accepting your correction. On completion the listener understands the error and decides how to act. Once per claim per conversation. The listener must be able to understand you.

Correct the Record II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Correct the Record adds 1/3/4 progress.

Correct the Record III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Correct the Record may address up to three listeners with separate acceptance objectives, using one roll.

Proof against Panic

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Reaction · Knowledge. When a group within 6 squares is about to act on an alarming claim or misunderstanding, offer a credible correction it can understand before it acts. Roll once; add 3/5/7 progress to up to four listeners’ separate correction objectives. A listener whose objective completes also reduces Frightened arising from that mistaken belief by 2. Once per distinct claim per scene; true danger, magical compulsion and player decisions are unaffected.

Languages

Patient Translation I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · 10 minutes · Knowledge, with a glossary or parallel text. Add 1/2/3 progress toward translating one short passage in an unfamiliar nonmagical language. A reference is required; ciphers need a separate objective.

Patient Translation II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Patient Translation adds 1/3/4 progress.

Patient Translation III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Patient Translation takes 5 minutes per attempt.

Bridge of Words I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · 10 minutes with a willing speaker and usable shared signs or reference text. Establish simple communication about directions, quantities and immediate needs for this conversation, without a roll. Abstract bargains and hidden meanings still require translation.

Bridge of Words II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Bridge of Words takes 5 minutes and can include up to three willing speakers who share the unfamiliar language.

Bridge of Words III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Once Bridge of Words is established, gain 1 Boon on translation rolls using notes or examples gathered from that conversation.

The Lost Lexicon

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 1 hour · Knowledge, with at least three substantial texts or a text and a willing fluent speaker. Add 3/5/7 progress toward reconstructing an unfamiliar nonmagical writing system. On completion create a working glossary that serves as a reference for Patient Translation for anyone who can read your notes. Missing vocabulary, ciphers and magical meanings remain separate questions; the glossary does not grant fluent speech.

Study your reserves, restore your focus and channel magical power.

Study Soul Capacity or Mind Capacity to increase the same SP reserve. When you learn either, add the printed increase to maximum SP and leave current SP as it is. Use Recovery to restore spent SP, up to your maximum. Study the Channeling spellbook to draw or share SP.

Soul Capacity

Soul Capacity I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Passive. Increase maximum SP by 2.

Soul Capacity II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Increase maximum SP by another 2; this path now grants +4 maximum SP.

Soul Capacity III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +7 maximum SP.

Deep Reserves I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Passive. Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +10 maximum SP.

Deep Reserves II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +13 maximum SP.

Deep Reserves III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +16 maximum SP.

Soul Wellspring

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Passive. Increase maximum SP by another 4; this path now grants +20 maximum SP. Once between safe overnight rests, when you spend SP to cast a spell, you may pay up to 2 of its SP from this reserve without reducing current SP. Declare the amount before casting; any unused part of that one payment is lost, not saved for another spell. This grants no additional casting or current-SP recovery.

Mind Capacity

Mind Capacity I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Passive. Increase maximum SP by 2.

Mind Capacity II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Increase maximum SP by another 2; this path now grants +4 maximum SP.

Mind Capacity III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +7 maximum SP.

Ordered Mind I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Passive. Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +10 maximum SP.

Ordered Mind II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +13 maximum SP.

Ordered Mind III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Increase maximum SP by another 3; this path now grants +16 maximum SP.

Mind Palace

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Passive. Increase maximum SP by another 4; this path now grants +20 maximum SP. Once between safe overnight rests, when you begin a ritual you have learned, reduce its total printed SP cost by 2, minimum 0. For a ritual with daily payments, reduce only its first payment. Declare before beginning; interruption still spends that benefit. Work time, materials and other requirements remain.

Recovery

Recovery I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 1 uninterrupted hour of safe rest, meditation or quiet leisure. Once between safe overnight rests, recover 1 SP. You can spend this hour during a Brief Rest and add this SP to what the rest restores.

Recovery II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 The same single recovery rest restores 2 SP in total.

Recovery III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 The same single recovery rest restores 3 SP in total.

Quiet Renewal I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 The same single recovery rest restores 4 SP in total. Learning this step does not grant another use if that rest has already been used.

Quiet Renewal II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 The same single recovery rest restores 6 SP in total.

Quiet Renewal III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 The same single recovery rest restores 8 SP in total.

Perfect Repose

DP: 5 | Level: 7 The same single recovery rest restores 12 SP in total and takes 30 uninterrupted minutes of safe rest or quiet leisure instead of an hour. It remains once between safe overnight rests and does not count as a safe overnight rest. No Grit, first-aid allowance or other limited use is refreshed.

Channeling

Learn the Channeling spellbook’s seven sections in order. Sections I–IV each teach two spells; V, VI and VII each teach one spell. Its spells transfer or recover SP using their own costs, targets and actions. A channeling spell cannot channel another channeling spell; attempting that transfer causes arcane feedback and provides no SP. Capacity training grants no channeling spell by itself.

Work between what people notice and what they assume.

Find cover, get your tools within reach and examine the mechanism or person you mean to outwit. The DA sets the objective and consequences before you roll. Work on components you can reach, and keep concealment between you and anyone watching. Use a Reaction when you perceive its stated trigger.

Locks

Patient Hand I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Guile, with lock tools. Examine and manipulate one reachable simple nonmagical fastening; add 1/2/3 progress toward opening it. The DA fixes the objective and work interval first: an intricate lock takes 10 minutes per attempt instead of a Main Action. Impossible mechanisms require another approach.

Patient Hand II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Patient Hand adds 1/3/4 progress.

Patient Hand III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Patient Hand takes 5 minutes rather than 10 on intricate locks.

Open under Pressure I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Guile, with lock tools. Work on a reachable nonmagical lock with accessible workings. Add 1/2/3 progress toward opening it.

Open under Pressure II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Open under Pressure adds 1/3/4 progress.

Open under Pressure III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Open under Pressure gains 1 Boon when you have both lock and repair tools at hand.

Silent Entry

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Guile for a simple fastening, or 1 minute for an intricate mechanism, with lock and repair tools. Add 3/5/7 progress toward opening one reachable nonmagical door, lock or fastening without visible damage. At completion you can close it to appear undisturbed to casual inspection. Separate alarms and traps remain separate tasks.

Sleight

Light Fingers I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver · Guile, with a free hand. Palm or plant one unattended palm-sized object within reach; add 1/2/3 progress toward doing so unnoticed. The DA sets the objective and whether scrutiny permits the attempt. The object moves when that objective completes.

Light Fingers II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Light Fingers adds 1/3/4 progress.

Light Fingers III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Light Fingers can also target an accessible object worn or carried by a distracted creature, other than a held weapon, secured container or worn armor.

Switch the Prize I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver · Guile. Exchange a reachable palm-sized object with a similar object you carry. Use Light Fingers’ requirements and add 1/3/4 progress toward this single unnoticed-exchange objective. The exchange occurs on completion.

Switch the Prize II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Switch the Prize gains 1 Boon when the replacement has been prepared to closely resemble the original.

Switch the Prize III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Switch the Prize can exchange an object up to the size of a closed book if you have two free hands and a suitable distraction; other restrictions remain.

The Perfect Substitution

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver · Guile during an ongoing conversation. Engage a listener who understands you while exchanging an accessible palm-sized object within reach for a similar object you carry. Roll once; add 2/4/6 progress to separately established deception and unnoticed-exchange objectives. The exchange occurs only when its own objective completes. Once per exchange, with a new plausible statement or distraction; repeating it unchanged gives no progress. Held weapons, armor and secured containers remain excluded.

Traps

Catch the Click I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction. When you see a nonmagical trap begin to trigger, warn one creature within 3 squares that can perceive you before its defense or avoidance roll; that roll gains 1 Boon. Once per triggering event. You can also inspect a suspected reachable trap for 1 minute, rolling Reason for 1/2/3 progress to identify its trigger and danger.

Catch the Click II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Catch the Click’s inspection adds 1/3/4 progress; its warning reaches 6 squares.

Catch the Click III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 After identifying a trap through that inspection, gain 1 Boon on Guile rolls to disarm it with suitable tools.

Turn the Trap I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction. When you notice a nonmagical trap trigger, guide one willing adjacent creature 1 square to a legal destination before the trap resolves. You can instead shift a reachable trigger you understand with tools in hand. This movement triggers no movement reactions; the trap then resolves normally at its actual area. Once per triggering event. You can also reconfigure an identified trap with 10 minutes and tools: roll Guile for 1/2/3 progress; completion establishes one reachable trigger or safe bypass without increasing damage or scale.

Turn the Trap II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Turn the Trap’s reconfiguration adds 1/3/4 progress.

Turn the Trap III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Turn the Trap can guide two willing adjacent creatures 1 square each before resolution, with separate legal destinations. Reaction: before your defense against an adjacent sighted attacker, scatter carried sand or grit with a free hand to gain 1 Boon on that defense. Consume the handful; once per attacker per scene. This grants no blindness condition and does not work on a creature that does not rely on sight.

Read the Killing Ground

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 10 minutes · Reason. Survey a visible area up to 6 squares across; add 3/5/7 progress to identify accessible nonmagical traps, triggers and a safe route. Completion reveals supported findings and inaccessible gaps. Companions following your exact unchanged route avoid triggering its identified traps. Reaction: when a companion within 6 squares starts to leave that route toward an identified trigger, warn it before the step; if it perceives you, it may cancel that step and choose another legal step using the same movement. Once per misstep; no extra movement.

Stealth

Quiet Passage I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Passive. Gain 1 Boon on Agility rolls to move quietly while concealed. Concealment needs cover or a plausible distraction.

Quiet Passage II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Quiet Passage removes extra movement cost imposed solely by sneaking.

Quiet Passage III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Quiet Passage extends its Boon to one willing adjacent companion moving with you through the same concealment.

Vanish into Cover I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver · Agility. Move up to 2 squares into cover, then add 1/2/3 progress toward evading pursuers. Become Hidden when the DA’s objective completes and concealment is plausible.

Vanish into Cover II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Vanish into Cover adds 1/3/4 progress.

Vanish into Cover III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Vanish into Cover moves up to 3 squares; this movement triggers no movement reactions from creatures that cannot see you when you begin moving.

The Hidden Road

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 1 hour · Agility, with rope and concealment materials. Establish a concealed route up to 20 squares long across terrain you can physically traverse; add 3/5/7 progress toward the DA’s route objective. On completion, up to six companions following your instructions can traverse it at normal movement cost with 2 Boons to remain unnoticed. It creates no unsupported bridge. Discovery or damage ends these benefits until the route is repaired and concealed again.

Read the fight, make a plan and put someone in position to use it.

Attacks from Tactics use Knowledge and require a wielded melee weapon. A willing ally can follow a cue if they perceive and understand your signal. Boons from Tactics and Aid do not add together on a single roll. Apply only the highest grant from those sources. A creature can hold the Boons from only one Tactics ability at a time. A new grant replaces the old ability’s unused Boons.

Openings

Exploit the Opening I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Knowledge. Attack one visible adjacent enemy for 1/3/4 physical damage. On Standard or Strong, cue one willing ally within 3 squares of you. That ally may move 1 square after the attack, following the usual movement reactions.

Exploit the Opening II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Exploit the Opening deals 2/4/5 physical damage.

Exploit the Opening III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Movement granted by Exploit the Opening avoids reactions from the target of your attack.

Divide Their Attention I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Knowledge. Attack one visible adjacent enemy for 2/4/6 physical damage. On Standard or Strong, choose one willing ally within 3 squares. It gains 1 Boon on its next attack against that enemy before your next turn starts.

Divide Their Attention II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Divide Their Attention deals 3/5/7 physical damage.

Divide Their Attention III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 On Strong, Divide Their Attention may grant its Boon to two willing allies within range.

Spring the Trap

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Knowledge. Once per scene, attack a visible adjacent enemy for 4/6/8 physical damage. On Standard or Strong, up to three willing allies within 4 squares may each move 2 squares, avoiding movement reactions from the target. Each gains 1 Boon on its next attack against that target before your next turn starts. On Strong, the target also gains Dazed 1.

Coordination

Clear the Way I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver. Give one willing ally within 3 squares a cue and choose attack or defense. The ally gains 1 Boon on its next roll of that type before your next turn starts. No roll.

Clear the Way II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Clear the Way reaches up to 5 squares.

Clear the Way III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Clear the Way can instead cue the ally for a chosen noncombat task. Its next roll for that task gains the Boon during the exchange or work interval. Outside combat, contribute this aid or your own roll to the objective during that interval.

Set the Formation I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver · Knowledge. Choose a visible enemy and up to two willing allies within 4 squares. On any result, one chosen ally may move 1 square without triggering movement reactions from that enemy. On Standard or Strong, each chosen ally gains 1 Boon on its next attack against that enemy before your next turn starts.

Set the Formation II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Set the Formation allows every chosen ally to move the square.

Set the Formation III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Set the Formation can choose up to three willing allies within range.

The Perfect Moment

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver · Knowledge. Once per scene, choose a visible enemy and up to three willing allies within 6 squares. Each ally may move 1/2/3 squares without triggering movement reactions from that enemy. Each gains 1 Boon on its next attack against that enemy before your next turn starts, or 2 Boons on Strong.

Contingencies

Call the Warning I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction. Before a willing ally within 3 squares rolls defense against an attack from an enemy you can see, give it 1 Boon on that defense if it can follow your cue. No separate roll.

Call the Warning II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Call the Warning reaches up to 5 squares.

Call the Warning III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 After a Strong defense aided by Call the Warning, the ally may move 1 square without triggering movement reactions from that attacker.

On My Signal I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction. When a visible enemy within 4 squares ends voluntary movement, cue one willing ally within 4 squares. It may move up to 2 squares without triggering movement reactions from that enemy. No roll.

On My Signal II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 On My Signal can cue two willing allies within range.

On My Signal III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Each ally moving with On My Signal may move up to 3 squares.

Roads Out

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Reaction. Once per scene, when a visible enemy within 6 squares ends voluntary movement, choose up to three willing allies within 6 squares. You and each chosen ally may move up to 3 squares without triggering movement reactions. Each chosen ally gains 1 Boon on its next defense against that enemy before your next turn starts. No roll.

Foresight

Read the Pattern I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver. Observe one visible enemy. Until your next turn starts, gain 1 Boon on the next attack you make against it or the next defense you roll against it, whichever comes first. No roll.

Read the Pattern II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 When you use Read the Pattern, you may first move 1 square. Follow the usual movement reactions.

Read the Pattern III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 You may choose whether to keep the Boon for an attack roll or a defense roll against the chosen enemy when you use Read the Pattern.

Rehearse the Exchange I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver · Knowledge. Study one visible enemy. Move up to 1 square, then gain 1 Boon on your next attack or next defense roll against it before your next turn starts. Choose which when you use this technique. On Strong, you may move up to 2 squares instead. Follow the usual movement reactions.

Rehearse the Exchange II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Rehearse the Exchange gives 2 Boons instead of 1 on Strong.

Rehearse the Exchange III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Movement from Rehearse the Exchange avoids movement reactions from the chosen enemy.

Three Moves Ahead

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver · Knowledge. Once per scene, choose up to two visible enemies. Move up to 2/3/4 squares without triggering movement reactions from them. Until your next turn starts, gain 2 Boons on your next attack against a chosen enemy and 1 Boon on your next defense against a chosen enemy. These are two distinct rolls. Taking this stance replaces any unused Boons from your other Tactics techniques.

Protect people and places; secure and unravel magic.

Read a living landscape and find your place within it.

Use real terrain, available resources and credible handling of animals. The DA sets objectives, accessible areas and hazards before rolls. Food and water gathering yields once per area per day for the whole party; repeated searches do not refill it. Animals retain their own motives.

Tracking

Read the Trail I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · Reason. Read tracks or signs immediately before you; add 1/2/3 progress toward identifying direction, approximate numbers and freshness. Following a trail to the next landmark takes 10 minutes per attempt instead. The DA defines each objective from accessible evidence.

Read the Trail II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Read the Trail adds 1/3/4 progress.

Read the Trail III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Read the Trail takes 5 minutes per attempt when following a trail.

Cut Them Off I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · Reason to interpret a visible junction on a readable trail, or 10 minutes to scout a wider interception route. Add 1/2/3 progress toward finding a physically feasible interception. Completion reveals the route and travel time, not a guarantee of arriving first.

Cut Them Off II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Cut Them Off adds 1/3/4 progress.

Cut Them Off III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 After completing Cut Them Off, you and up to four companions gain 1 Boon on travel rolls to traverse that identified route until its next landmark. Changed or blocked terrain requires a new route.

Unerring Pursuit

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · Reason at a visible junction, or 10 minutes to scout the surrounding area. From a trail you can read, add 3/5/7 progress toward predicting the quarry’s next reachable landmark from its tracks and known terrain. Completion identifies the best-supported destination and gaps in the evidence. You and up to six companions gain 2 Boons on pursuit and traversal rolls along that route until reaching it. This does not locate a quarry that left no readable evidence.

Animal Handling

Gentle Hand I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Maneuver · Reason. Reassure one nonmagical animal within 2 squares that can perceive you and add 1/2/3 progress toward calming its fear. Spend a Maneuver with a receptive animal or 1 minute per attempt with a wary or agitated one. Find an approach it can respond to in the circumstances.

Gentle Hand II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Gentle Hand adds 1/3/4 progress.

Gentle Hand III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Gentle Hand may address three animals sharing the same cause of agitation as one objective.

Lead the Herd I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Maneuver · Reason. Direct up to six calm nonmagical animals already cooperating with you toward a visible safe route; add 1/2/3 progress to the DA’s handling objective. Establishing initial cooperation takes 10 minutes per attempt instead. Completion gets them moving with you; danger or mistreatment ends cooperation.

Lead the Herd II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Lead the Herd adds 1/3/4 progress.

Lead the Herd III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Lead the Herd can guide twelve calm animals, and you gain 1 Boon on handling rolls to keep that herd together in ordinary travel.

Wild Accord

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Maneuver · Reason. Give up to twelve nonmagical animals that can perceive you one understandable direction: follow, wait, scatter to safety or approach a named visible place. For a group that needs coaxing, add 3/5/7 progress to the DA’s handling objective. A group already cooperating follows a safe instruction without a roll. Completion gets the group carrying out that direction. This grants no attacks or additional combat turns; serious danger or mistreatment ends cooperation.

Trailcraft

Trail Warning I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Reaction. When a visible natural hazard begins to threaten a companion within 3 squares, before its avoidance roll, warn it. If it can perceive you, that roll gains 1 Boon. The hazard must be something you can observe, such as shifting footing or a falling branch. Once per hazard event.

Trail Warning II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Trail Warning reaches 6 squares.

Trail Warning III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Trail Warning may aid two companions affected by the same hazard, each before its roll.

Turn Back the Danger I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Reaction. When a visible natural hazard is about to affect one willing companion within 3 squares, guide it up to 1 square along a legal safe route before resolution if it perceives you. This triggers no movement reactions. Resolve the hazard at its actual location afterward; it gains 1 Boon on any remaining avoidance roll. Once per hazard event.

Turn Back the Danger II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Turn Back the Danger reaches 6 squares.

Turn Back the Danger III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 Turn Back the Danger can guide two willing companions, each to a separate legal square, and grants 2 Boons to their remaining avoidance rolls.

Safe Passage

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Reaction. When one visible natural hazard threatens a group within 6 squares, warn up to six willing companions who can perceive you. Each may move up to 2 squares along a legal route you can see before the hazard resolves, without movement reactions. Each gains 2 Boons on any remaining avoidance roll against that event. Once per hazard event; it does not cancel the hazard, cross impassable terrain or reveal hidden threats.

Provisioning

Wild Harvest I

DP: 1 | Level: 1 Main Action · 1 hour · Knowledge. Search an accessible area for food or drinkable water. The DA defines the area and confirms a plausible source before you roll. Raise one Food Bundle or Water Flask of the chosen type by 1/2/3 supply die steps, maximum d8. An empty supply starts at d4 on the first step. You can also spend 1 hour with available materials to shelter two people from ordinary rain and wind, without a roll.

Wild Harvest II

DP: 2 | Level: 1 Wild Harvest raises the supply by 2/3/4 steps, maximum d8. Its ordinary shelter accommodates four people.

Wild Harvest III

DP: 2 | Level: 1 When you find both sources, Wild Harvest can raise one Food Bundle and one Water Flask in the same hour. Apply the rolled steps to each. Its ordinary shelter takes 30 minutes.

A Camp without a Trace I

DP: 3 | Level: 3 Main Action · 30 minutes · Guile. Conceal a completed camp and its approach; add 1/2/3 progress to the DA’s concealment objective. Completion hides casual signs; direct search remains possible. You can also search water-bearing terrain for 1 hour, rolling Reason for 1/2/3 progress toward finding a concealed spring; completion reveals its location and visible hazards, not purification.

A Camp without a Trace II

DP: 4 | Level: 3 A Camp without a Trace adds 1/3/4 progress to concealment and spring searches.

A Camp without a Trace III

DP: 4 | Level: 3 A Camp without a Trace’s ordinary shelter accommodates six people, and concealment attempts take 15 minutes instead of 30.

Shelter against the Siege

DP: 5 | Level: 7 Main Action · 1 hour, with tools and enough sound structural and concealment materials. Build a concealed fortified shelter for up to eight people on stable ground. No roll. Occupants behind its walls gain 2 Boons on defense against attacks from outside; each door or wall section has 15 HP and physical resistance 2. Open doors provide no protection. The shelter does not automatically make overnight rest safe; ordinary object damage rules apply.

Your culture, background and class each give you a discipline to study. To begin another, spend the 1, 2 or 3 DP listed for your class. Choose a path in that discipline and learn its entries in order, paying the listed DP. You can study several paths. To learn an entry, meet its level requirement and learn the earlier entries in that path.

When you learn an improvement, apply it along with the benefits you already learned for that ability. If it gives a new value for damage, range or another number, use that value in place of the old one. Advanced entries become available at level 3 and masteries at level 7. Read each entry to see whether it teaches a new ability or improves one you already know.

To study a spellbook, learn its sections in order and add the spells marked for each section. See @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.895ef20bc4923b2e.JournalEntryPage.684bcf0a86d4b4b4]{Magic and spellbooks} for the section costs and levels. In Spellcraft, study Soul Capacity or Mind Capacity to hold more SP, Recovery to restore spent SP, or Channeling to transfer it.

Every hero can make basic attacks, speak, climb, search and help. Learned abilities give you more ways to act. Read their requirements and gather any gear you need.

Common action rules

Damage and progress written as three numbers mean Weak / Standard / Strong. Roll 3d6 plus the stated attribute, applying normal Boons and Banes: Weak is 8 or less, Standard 9–14, Strong 15 or more. For attacks against your hero, you roll the printed defense. For exchanges between NPCs, a player or the DA rolls using the NPC procedure.

Every attack hits. Remove immune damage types, then apply weakness, matching resistance and other reductions. Keep the final minimum of 1 if any positive damage component survived immunity. Reducing a condition or forced movement to 0 is permitted: those are not damage. Attack damage is instant; conditions follow their normal timing and decay unless an ability states a duration. Stability and any explicit forced-movement defenses still apply.

An ability costs its printed action every time it is used. Spend an available Reaction when its stated trigger occurs. Outside combat, follow the ability’s limit per exchange, task or event. An improvement costs no separate action unless stated. Passive training works while its requirements hold. A time such as 10 minutes is the uninterrupted work required for each roll; it is not a combat Main Action. Normal condition restrictions and action conversions still apply.

Targets must be reachable as the ability describes. Movement requires an unoccupied legal destination and a feasible route; it stops at barriers. When forced movement meets a creature or barrier, use the collision rules in Playing the Game. Other movement uses the usual movement-reaction rules unless the entry explicitly avoids them. An ability with a choice of up to several targets can affect each target only once per use.

Gather the equipment your chosen technique uses. An entry that provides equipment describes what you receive. Use the inventory and price rules for recipes and ingredients. Smoke ingredients use one ordinary recipe ingredient batch per flask, with price and availability set before preparation; finished flasks have Bulk 1 each. Prepared products persist until used or spoiled. Craft covers ordinary construction and preparation; use the appropriate magical working to create enchanted items.

For tasks that take several contributions, use Objectives and progress in the play procedures. For first aid, treatment and rest, see the recovery chapter.

A spellbook gathers a related family of spells. Its colored rows show the sections you learn as your studies deepen; each learned section adds spells to your repertoire.

Casting a spell

Choose a learned spell and legal targets, and commit its stated action. Resolve any opportunity attack first. If you can continue, recheck your targets, pay the printed SP and resolve the spell. You need a free hand and a clear path to a target unless the spell describes a remote connection. A spell that names a held weapon or shield as its casting focus uses that item to fulfill the free-hand requirement. Measure range in squares from your position to the target or chosen point. Use the range given in the spell block. A point or destination must be visible when chosen unless the spell explicitly uses a known place, memory, object or person instead. Carry ordinary gear within your usual capacity when a spell transports you.

When you roll to cast, use the casting attribute listed by your class. A spell block marked Class uses that attribute. An Arcanist casting Fire Bolt rolls Knowledge; a Shadow casting it rolls Guile. Use any separate Defense, Hold or Escape attribute when that roll is called for. A block marked Automatic resolves its stated effect directly. Three values always mean Weak / Standard / Strong. Attacks use the familiar 3d6 resolution and the normal rules for immunity, resistance and minimum damage. Apply a condition at its listed rating unless the target is immune to that condition, then use its normal timing and decay. Apply healing after the recipient's Life resistance, restore at least 1 HP when HP is missing, and stop at maximum HP. Healing spends SP independently of the recipient's first-aid treatment.

For several targets, work out the relevant Boons and Banes for each, roll once using the combination least favorable to you, and apply the result to every target. A spell that says every creature includes allies. A spell that says choose or up to a number lets you select its recipients. Affect each creature once per casting, even if it occupies several squares in the area. A cone widens from your square to the stated width at its far edge; a line is one square wide. Count radius distance using normal grid distance.

Players make the rolls. When an NPC casts against heroes, each affected player rolls the appropriate defense: Fortitude against bodily alteration, poison or life drain; Agility against aimed rays, bursts and moving hazards; Reason against thought, emotion, divination or magical binding. A spell or creature profile may name a more specific defense. Read the caster's outcomes in reverse: a Weak defense receives its Strong effect, Standard receives Standard, and Strong receives Weak. For an NPC-only exchange use the ordinary DA resolution procedure. Resolve automatic environmental and willing effects as printed.

Actions and Rituals

Main Action spells include attacks, substantial healing, battlefield control and summoning. Attack cantrips also use a Main Action. Maneuver spells handle brief, small effects, such as sending a message, lighting an object or moving a small item. The action printed in each spell is the procedure to use.

A Reaction spell names its trigger and when to respond. Spend your available Reaction when that event occurs. A defense bonus applies before the roll; a reduction or redirection applies at the timing stated in its block. The ordinary action conversions still apply to casting, including using a Main Action for a Maneuver spell.

A Ritual is a Main Action that takes its full printed casting time, usually outside combat. Pay SP and supply any listed materials at the beginning, following a printed daily schedule or payment timing when given. Work continuously for the stated time or scheduled work period, keeping the required subjects and materials present. Finish the Ritual before receiving its effect. An interrupted Ritual must be started again with fresh costs. Ritual work is active activity rather than restorative rest. Materials described as consumed are used up by the attempt at the printed time, or at the beginning when no time is given.

Duration and sustained magic

An instant spell resolves once. A fixed-duration spell lasts for its printed time. In combat, count 10 rounds for each minute. You may end your own ongoing spell with a Maneuver. When it changes ordinary material permanently, the resulting object or terrain follows ordinary rules afterward. A magical effect ending leaves its described consequences in place: healed HP stays restored and damage stays dealt.

For a spell marked Sustained, casting maintains it until the end of your next turn. Starting on the turn after you cast it, spend a Maneuver and 0 SP by the end of each turn to maintain it through the end of your following turn, within the printed maximum duration. Perform that upkeep once per turn. A Main Action may convert to the required Maneuver. The upkeep's listed movement or renewal is part of that same Maneuver. A separate attack or other activity that names a Main Action still uses it.

You may sustain one spell at a time. Beginning another sustained spell ends the previous one. Unconsciousness, death, or missing an upkeep ends sustain. If a block says a condition is renewed, raise that spell's remaining contribution to the named rating rather than adding another instance each round. Conditions decay normally after renewal ends.

Identical named ongoing benefits on one recipient use the strongest value and the latest expiry; repeated castings refresh rather than multiply the benefit. Each independent damaging zone follows its stated per-round limit. Resolve damage when entering or ending a turn in such a zone, as printed; forced movement can cause entry. A round begins with the first creature's turn and ends after the last creature's turn.

Lasting magic and directing an effect

A fixed-duration spell remains for its printed time without Sustain. Some spells let you direct an existing effect with a Maneuver or Main Action. That action moves or uses it; omitting the action leaves it in place unless the spell says otherwise. A commanded summoned form uses its command procedure, not both commands and Sustain.

A creature forced into a damaging zone triggers its entry effect just as one walking into it would; moving a zone over a creature counts as entry when its spell says so. Apply the printed once-per-round limit across the whole casting, not once per square. Count any damage on creation toward that limit. Continuing environmental damage is not a new attack and matching resistance can reduce it to 0. An actual attack named by the spell still uses the attack minimum.

For a player-created zone, retain its casting result for later automatic damage when instructed. For an NPC-created zone or triggered inscription, each affected hero rolls the printed defense when the harmful event occurs and reads the NPC's bands in reverse; do not roll for the NPC or substitute another hero's result. Apply the same per-creature trigger limit. A printed automatic event, such as touching an already heated item, uses its stated number instead of another attack roll.

Breaking a magical hold

Use your class’s casting attribute for the initial casting roll. Defense names the hero's initial defense against an NPC casting. Hold attribute names the player caster's roll when an NPC struggles free; Escape attribute names the player target's roll when escaping an NPC's hold. Use the attribute for the attempt you are making, even when it differs from the one used to cast the spell.

A conscious held target may spend a Main Action on its turn to attempt escape, even when the hold restricts its ordinary actions. This permission overrides the hold, not separate unconsciousness. When an NPC struggles against your spell, roll its printed Hold attribute: on Weak, that NPC breaks free; on Standard or Strong the hold remains. This response spends no action of yours. When your hero struggles against an NPC spell, roll its printed Escape attribute: on Strong, your hero breaks free; on Weak or Standard the hold remains. Players still apply appropriate Boons and Banes. For NPC-only exchanges use the existing DA procedure.

Escape removes only that casting's hold on that target. Other targets and independent conditions remain. Once free, use any movement, Maneuver or Reaction still available. Sustaining the spell and answering an escape attempt are different events: no automatic escape roll or extra SP payment occurs during upkeep. Physical Grappled 3 retains its own release rules; a spell's escape permission applies to its named magical hold.

For example, Entangle is cast with Reason. Against an NPC casting, the hero initially defends with Agility. An NPC spending its Main Action to escape a hero's roots makes that hero roll Reason to keep the hold; Weak frees the NPC. A hero caught by an NPC's roots instead spends a Main Action and rolls Agility; Strong frees the hero. Hold Person uses Reason for all four fields because its bindings answer mental resolve rather than a physical gap.

Summons, forms and invitations

A spell that creates a summoned form uses its listed profile, one immediate Main command on arrival, continuing commands and the six-square tether from Summoned Companions. Commands maintain these forms for the printed duration; they use the command procedure rather than sustained-spell upkeep. Their HP tracks the form, and they disperse at 0 HP or when their controller becomes unconscious or dies. Healing they perform spends the controller's SP. Summoned forms receive activity through commands and return to energy when their duration ends.

The roster's ratings 1, 3 and 7 describe which profiles a calling can produce. The spell names its permitted category and maximum rating. Use the summoned profile rather than the DA creature's combat entry. Animal shapes worn by a hero instead keep that hero's HP, attributes and resources, using the spell's stated movement and natural attacks.

A Familiar bond or invitation to a named planar being concerns an independent creature. It keeps its own needs, choices and relationships. Negotiate its service through the ordinary social procedures. A resurrection restores the named person only with that person's agreement. Lifegiving and True Resurrection share one lifetime return per person; Grit is separate.

Illusions and informed choices

An illusion creates the sights, sounds or sensations its block describes. Physical interaction reveals an insubstantial image. To study a plausible illusion by observation, a hero spends a Main Action and rolls Reason for 1/2/3 progress toward target 3. Once complete, the hero recognizes it. When an NPC examines a hero's illusion, the player rolls Guile and the observer gains 3/2/1 progress on the player's Weak/Standard/Strong result. Keep that observer's progress for that illusion. Sound alone reveals no physical barrier or support.

Mental and social spells state the information, progress, conditions or choices they provide. Use the social objective procedure for concessions, with the DA setting a feasible goal around the listener's motives. A hero's player supplies their character's private thoughts or chooses their response where the spell calls for one. A spell that offers a command or resistance effect gives that choice to the target's controller.

Unraveling a spell

Cancellation is progress against a particular casting. Its target is 2 + the spell's printed SP cost, unless the effect states its own remedy. Use the target of the affected spell rather than any extra SP spent transferring it. Keep accumulated progress while that same casting remains active. Completing the objective ends that casting; incomplete progress expires when it ends. A Reaction that interrupts casting must reach its target during that trigger to prevent resolution. Its block states any partial effect.

Spellbook spells, including Rituals, may be unraveled when the cancellation entry can reach and identify the effect. Removing a lasting enchantment follows its explicit remedy or Unessence. A specific remedy such as Remove Curse may end an effect immediately when the effect says so. Ordinary material shaped by a completed spell remains an ordinary object afterward.

Sharing Spell Points

Casting costs are paid separately from any SP moved. Sustain costs a Maneuver and 0 SP; transferred points still leave the donor’s reserve. Transfer existing points from a donor's current reserve into a recipient's missing SP; the amount moved is the smallest of the spell's limit, the donor's available points, and the recipient's remaining capacity. Subtract the exact amount received from the donor. A reserve of 0 transfers 0.

Choose two different personal reserves for a transfer. A summoned form, animated group or magical duplicate uses its controller's resource rules and provides no independent SP reserve. A willing donor chooses its contribution. For unwilling participants, use the printed roll and the ordinary player-facing defense procedure; transferred SP itself causes no HP damage. A redirected transfer resolves once to its final recipient.

A transmitted spell uses its own action category and costs as stated by the channeling block. Its original caster makes any casting roll and handles sustain; the releasing ally uses the named Reaction. Rituals retain their full ritual time and preparation, and are outside effects that explicitly transmit a Main Action spell.

Choose a spell from outside the Channeling book when you use Channel Spell or Lord Channels. Channeling one of the book's own spells would send the magic back as arcane feedback.

Begin studying a discipline at the price listed for your class, then choose a path or spellbook and learn its entries. Each reference gives the effects, costs and learning order.
